messages:
carmen_peopleops: Hey team — got a carrier denial on dependent documentation for OE. They flagged my 23yo as ineligible and said the student affidavit was insufficient. OE window closes in 9 days. What can we do fast?

ivan_benefits: Sorry about that, @carmen_peopleops. Which carrier sent the denial and what reason code did they give? Sometimes they want a more detailed enrollment letter or proof of full-time status for the specific plan year.

carmen_peopleops: Carrier: AcmeHealth. Denial reason: "Insufficient proof of full-time student status" and note says docs not dated within 30 days of submission. I uploaded a letter dated 2026-07-01 but carrier says they needed a 2026-08-15 dated letter for fall term verification.

rafaela_oe: For OE we treat dependent documentation a bit differently: if the carrier denies during OE, we can submit an appeal to the carrier and provide a supplementary affidavit plus a screenshot of the student's full-time course load from the university portal (if available).

matt_payroll: Timeline note: if the dependent is rejected for OE, premiums billed for the upcoming plan year will be reversed once the appeal is approved, but appeals can take 7-21 business days depending on carrier. If you need coverage immediately, we can provisionally keep them on the plan for 30 days pending appeal if you request an expedited review. That would avoid a gap but may require you to attest in writing.

benefits-bot: To file an appeal or upload additional docs: https://benefits.redwood.com/docs-upload -> choose "OE dependent appeal". Please include denial letter, new dated proof, and a signed affidavit. Deadline for appeal: within 30 days of denial.

ivan_benefits: If you can get a stamped enrollment letter from the university registrar showing start date and term load and with a recent date (within 14 days), that usually satisfies AcmeHealth. An alternate is a course schedule screenshot showing enrollment status plus payment receipt for the term.

carmen_peopleops: University registrar is closed this week for term break. Student can get a screenshot from the student portal but Im worried about carrier rejecting screenshots. Would a notarized affidavit from the student plus the portal screenshot work?

rafaela_oe: Yes, a notarized affidavit + screenshot + the original OO enrollment form usually passes. Also attach a statement from you confirming dependent is claimed on your household during OE. We can bundle into an appeal packet.

matt_payroll: If you want provisional coverage during appeal, reply here with "PROVISIONAL ON" and we'll flag payroll and benefits to hold premium changes. Note: provisional coverage is reversible if appeal fails and results in a retro deduction.

carmen_peopleops: Okay, doing provisional. PROVISIONAL ON. Also uploading a notarized affidavit tonight and portal screenshot.

ivan_benefits: Case opened: OE-AP-2026-7783. I'll submit the appeal to AcmeHealth once you upload the extra docs. Please include student ID, dependent DOB, and the portal screenshot with timestamp or page footer showing date.

benefits-bot: Upload link: https://benefits.redwood.com/docs-upload (case OE-AP-2026-7783). Carrier appeal ETA: 7-14 business days. If expedited, add note "EXPEDITE - closes in X days".

carmen_peopleops: Uploaded affidavit + screenshot. Marking as expedite (open enrollment closes in 9 days). Thanks for the help.

ivan_benefits: Got it. Ill note "EXPEDITE - OE CLOSE" and push the appeal. If carrier requests additional verification well DM you the exact wording to request from the registrar. For payroll: @matt_payroll will hold provisional premiums for now.

matt_payroll: Noted. Provisional flag set. Well hold the premium line and not reverse paychecks until appeal decision. If appeal denied, we will notify you and set up retro deduction options.

carmen_peopleops: Appreciate it. Fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:
